deterministic.name: check-runtime-contract-strings.py
deterministic.evidence: Applied manually from the frozen workbook Deterministic Checks sheet and skill references/deterministic-checks.md; the private checker executable was not available or run. Port 3000 agrees across test.sh lines 48, 109, 136 and 164 (127.0.0.1:3000, PORT="3000"), every prompt line 1 (http://localhost:3000), app_context.md line 4 and integration.md line 3 ("0.0.0.0 port 3000"). The liveness path GET /api/health is stated in integration.md line 3. Env vars: test.sh lines 104-109 inject PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME, PORT and DB_PATH, but the public brief and notes name only NODE_PATH and DB_PATH. PORT is never named as a variable (only "port 3000"), and neither HOME (set to /tmp/submission, not /app) nor PATH is named anywhere the agent reads.
deterministic.counterexample: A checker or reviewer that applies "env vars test.sh injects are named" literally will find PORT, HOME and PATH unnamed in instruction.md and /instructions. An app that resolves files or writes scratch data under $HOME would also not know that HOME is /tmp/submission. The sister task colderwater-playground-devtools names them in integration.md line 7 ("The launch environment supplies PORT=3000, NODE_PATH=... and PATH=...; HOME is a writable staging directory..."). The private checker may whitelist PATH/HOME and match "port" case-insensitively, so this is a credible but unconfirmed portal flag (P2).
deterministic.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to environment/instructions/integration.md naming the launch environment: PORT=3000, NODE_PATH, PATH, a HOME that may differ from /app, and DB_PATH.
